method: Rebuild from primary text. Bus. & Prof. Code Article 9 (§§17600-17606) was fetched in full from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov and read, including §§17601 and 17602 as amended by Stats. 2024, Ch. 515 (AB 2863), which the previous body was entirely silent about. The construing case was located through CourtListener. Assertions describe the REBUILT body.
queries: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §§17600-17606 full text (leginfo)
"17602" automatic renewal continuous service unconditional gift private right of action

assertions.text: the article reaches offers made to a consumer, defined as an individual acquiring goods, services, money or credit for personal, family or household purposes
assertions.note: §17601(a)(4), verbatim. The previous body said the clause applies where the renewal 'reaches a California consumer or small business offering'. A small business offering is not within the article at all. That is an overstatement of scope in a clause whose whole job is to tell a business what it must do.

assertions.text: the offer terms must be clear and conspicuous, presented before the agreement is fulfilled and in visual (or, for voice, temporal) proximity to the request for consent
assertions.note: §17602(a)(1). 'Clear and conspicuous' is itself defined in §17601(a)(3) in terms of type size, contrast and setting-off.

assertions.text: express affirmative consent to the offer terms is required, nothing in the contract may undermine the ability to give it, and an acknowledgment with the terms, the cancellation policy and how to cancel must be retainable
verification of consent must be kept at least three years, or one year after termination, whichever is longer
a pre-renewal notice is required in exactly two cases, with the timing windows stated
assertions.note: §17602(b)(1)-(2): a free gift or trial, or a promotional or discounted price, lasting more than 31 days — notice at least 3 and at most 21 days before it expires; or an initial term of one year or longer — notice at least 15 and not more than 45 days before renewal. The previous body said 'advance notice be given before a renewal following a free or discounted trial' with no 31-day qualifier, no window, and no mention of the one-year case at all.

assertions.text: a consumer who signed up online must be able to cancel exclusively online by a prominent direct link or button or a pre-formatted termination email, and cancellation must be available in the medium used to sign up
assertions.note: §17602(d)(1) and (f). The previous body had 'cancellation be available by the same medium used to sign up and be no more difficult than signing up', which is the pre-amendment formulation.

assertions.text: a retention offer may be presented only alongside a 'click to cancel' link online, or by telephone only after the consumer is told they may cancel at any time by saying so
a material change requires notice with cancellation information, and a fee change requires notice no less than 7 and no more than 30 days before it takes effect
an annual reminder is required on an annual plan, stating the product, the frequency and amount of charges, and how to cancel
goods sent without first obtaining affirmative consent are deemed an unconditional gift, and that consequence attaches to goods and to the absence of consent, not to every non-compliance
assertions.note: §17603, verbatim, and Mayron describes it as 'only a passive right to retain any products received from a violator'. The previous body said 'Goods delivered under a non-compliant automatic renewal may be treated as an unconditional gift', which is close but widens the trigger from absence of consent to non-compliance generally.

assertions.text: a business that complies with the article in good faith is not subject to civil remedies
assertions.note: §17604(b), verbatim. Absent from the previous body, and it is the only provision in the article that helps the business the clause is drafted for.

assertions.text: there is no private right of action under the article
assertions.note: Mayron v. Google LLC, quoted below. This contradicts the clause's stated rationale, which asserted that 'the statute carries a private right of action'. It is the clearest instance in this batch of a construction that changes what the words mean: §17604(a) says 'all available civil remedies that apply to a violation of this article may be employed', and the court held that is not the clear, unmistakable expression the Legislature must give.

assertions.text: the AB 2863 amendments apply only to a contract entered into, amended or extended on or after July 1, 2025
the article exempts six categories of entity
assertions.note: §17605(a)-(f): CPUC-franchised or -licensed services and their affiliates; entities regulated by the CPUC, FCC or FERC; entities regulated by the Department of Insurance; alarm company operators; banks, bank holding companies and licensed financial institutions; and regulated service contract sellers and administrators.

priorDefects: contradicted (rationale): 'the statute carries a private right of action'. Mayron v. Google LLC: 'We conclude there is no private right of action for violation of the automatic renewal law.'
overstated-scope: the clause applied the article to 'a California consumer or small business offering'. §17601(a)(4) limits it to consumers.

omitted: everything AB 2863 added — the free-to-pay conversion definition, the consent-verification retention period, the two pre-renewal notice cases with their windows, click-to-cancel and its email alternative, the retention-offer rules, the fee-change notice and the annual reminder.
omitted: the good faith safe harbour in §17604(b).
omitted: the July 1, 2025 application date for the amendments.
imprecise: the unconditional gift consequence in §17603 attaches to goods sent without affirmative consent, not to a 'non-compliant automatic renewal' generally.
gaps: The clause is inserted whenever the agreement auto-renews and the counterparty is Californian. Because the article reaches only consumers, that condition fires it for business-to-business agreements it does not govern. The rebuilt body says so in its first sentence rather than changing the condition, which is an engine change nobody has approved.
No decision construing §17604(b)'s good faith safe harbour was read, and its scope is the kind of thing decided by case law rather than text.
The federal Restore Online Shoppers' Confidence Act and any FTC negative-option rule were not read. A national subscription business needs both, and the clause says nothing about either.
Mayron predates AB 2863. Whether the 2024 amendments changed anything bearing on a private right of action was not researched; nothing read in §§17600-17606 creates one.

judicialQuotations.case: Mayron v. Google LLC (Cal. Ct. App. 2020)
judicialQuotations.quote: We conclude there is no private right of action for violation of the automatic renewal law. Further, since plaintiff has not alleged an injury caused by Google's conduct, he has no standing to sue under the unfair competition statute.

judicialQuotations.case: Mayron v. Google LLC (Cal. Ct. App. 2020)
judicialQuotations.quote: Seeing no clear indication of intent to create a private right of action in either the statutory text or its legislative history, we conclude there is no such right under the automatic renewal law. ... But the automatic renewal law can be enforced with an action brought by the Attorney General. A private individual can also pursue enforcemen...

judicialQuotations.case: Mayron v. Google LLC (Cal. Ct. App. 2020) — on §17603
judicialQuotations.quote: Section 17603 is different because it provides only a passive right to retain any products received from a violator, rather than a right to pursue a refund of fees a claimant could show had been paid.

currencyCaveat: Mayron is a 2020 decision and construes the article as it then stood. AB 2863 rewrote §§17601 and 17602 with effect for contracts entered into, amended or extended on or after July 1, 2025, but left §§17603 and 17604 — the two sections Mayron actually construed — untouched. The second quotation is truncated in the source excerpt at 'pursue enforcemen...' and should be re-read in full before it is quoted where a reader will rely on it.
